title: Docs + runbook updates for Incident Bot v2 diagnostics (deploy/config/saturation) + troubleshooting
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Update the on-call playbooks/runbooks to match Incident Bot v2 behavior and data sources. Add a troubleshooting section for missing/empty context cards (permissions, timeouts, degraded mode), and publish/centralize references to the ADR + incident context standards so responders have a single canonical place to start.

Why now:
- Beta rotations reported confusion on what is “expected” in the first 5 minutes and what to do when cards are empty.
- GA rollout requires clear guidance on deploy vs config vs saturation interpretation, plus explicit guidance on redaction/audit boundaries.

Scope includes:
- On-call playbook updates for using context cards.
- Runbooks: recent deploy context, config diff interpretation, GPU/queue/KV cache saturation triage.
- Troubleshooting: empty cards, partial outage behavior, query timeouts, rate limiting/load shedding, and break-glass access.
- Link to standards/ADR and ensure all docs use consistent field names and dashboard link formats.

Out of scope:
- Rewriting the incident process, status page changes, or new observability dashboards (handled in other tickets/PRs).
acceptance_criteria:
1) #incidents / #eng-oncall responders have a single “Incident Bot v2: first 5 minutes” playbook page that matches current bot cards and interactive actions.
2) Each card type (Recent deploys, Config diff, Saturation signals, Error budget burn links) has a short “How to interpret” section and “What to do next” actions.
3) Troubleshooting section covers: missing scope/permissions, telemetry query timeouts, degraded-mode behavior (cached context + links), and manual fallback commands.
4) Docs explicitly call out redaction + audit logging expectations and the break-glass path for Sev0/Sev1.
5) All pages reference the canonical standards/ADR and use the standardized payload field names and deep-link formats.
6) Docs PR merged (internal docs repo) before Incident Bot v2 GA announcement.
implementation_plan:
Plan
A) Update “Incident bot triage playbook”:
- Add a “First 5 minutes: check these 4 cards” checklist.
- Add guidance on which signals are most actionable by incident class (deploy regression vs misconfig vs regional saturation).
- Add “Verify before acting” notes (staged rollouts, partial propagation, config diff baseline selection).

B) Update runbooks:
- Recent deploys + config diff debugging: add examples of staged rollouts, rollbacks, canary vs full, and how to interpret rollout phase.
- GPU saturation triage: map GPU util vs queue depth vs KV cache pressure vs scheduler backpressure to likely causes and mitigations.

C) Add troubleshooting page/section:
- Symptom: empty cards → check bot scopes, thread permissions, tenant access, and audit events.
- Symptom: “timed out” / “degraded mode” → cached context behavior, links to dashboards, manual query commands.
- Symptom: diff shows many fields redacted → explain allowlist model, how to request elevated access, and break-glass procedure.

D) Standards and ADR references:
- Ensure each doc links to the incident context collection guidelines and ADR-013.
- Add a short “Data sources + permissions” section that matches the ADR (deploy metadata service, config diff endpoint, telemetry query service).

E) Publishing:
- Link docs from the bot output (where possible) and from the #incidents channel topic.
- Ensure searchability: include “incident-bot v2”, “context card”, “degraded mode”, “config diff”, “saturation signals” keywords.
manual_fallback_commands:
Suggested manual fallback commands/snippets to include in docs (final wording may differ based on tool availability):
- /incident-bot context --service <svc> --region <region> --tenant <tenant> --since 30m
- /incident-bot deploys --service <svc> --region <region> --since 6h
- /incident-bot config-diff --tenant <tenant> --service <svc> --since 2h --safe
- /incident-bot saturation --service <svc> --region <region> --since 30m
- If bot is degraded: use Console deep links for saturation overview + error budget burn, and follow the “GPU saturation triage” runbook.
risk_notes: Docs must not include sensitive tenant examples or any unredacted config fields. Use synthetic examples only. Ensure troubleshooting does not teach “workarounds” that bypass audit logging (all break-glass paths must be auditable).
